Looking at this question about 2pSAM (Two-photon Synthetic Aperture Microscopy), I need to recall the specific volumetric imaging rate reported for this technique.

2pSAM combines two-photon excitation with synthetic aperture methods to enable faster volumetric imaging. The technique achieves its speed by using computational reconstruction from multiple acquisition angles rather than mechanical scanning of the entire volume.

From the literature on 2pSAM, the net rate of 3D imaging for time-lapse continuous data was reported as 16 volumes/s.

[ANSWER]D[/ANSWER]
